channel.title: The College Fix - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The College Fix (thecollegefix.com)

item.title: Are books trendy again? Gen Z is buying more paperbacks, starting campus reading clubs
item.description: Gen Z is buying more print books than Millennials, and some are starting book clubs on their campuses. The University of Miami also recently reported a resurgence in reading books for pleasure.

item.title: Judge tosses case claiming Northwestern Law discriminated against white men
item.description: Despite the loss in court, Northwestern University in December agreed to pay $75 million to resolve a federal anti-discrimination probe. As part of the settlement, the university agreed to end all affirmative action policies.

item.title: Texas A&M ends women’s and gender studies degrees
item.description: 'The decision reflected both the requirements of System policies and limited student interest in the program based on enrollment over the past several years.'

item.title: ‘Significant harm’: Stanford student gov’t endorses anti-ICE walkout
item.description: ICE has 'history of inflicting significant harm,' Stanford student government says.

item.title: Trio of Minnesota law professors decry arrest of Don Lemon: ‘attack on free press’
item.description: Three Minnesota law professors criticized the arrests of Don Lemon and journalist Georgia Fort as an "attack on free press." They argue the use of the FACE Act against them is unprecedented and stifles journalism, contending such actions by the Trump administration aim to intimidate reporters from covering legitimate news events.

item.title: UNC System may cut student legal aid offices’ funding
item.description: The University of North Carolina is proposing to defund student legal aid offices in an effort to cut costs.

item.title: Racism complaint about UC Berkeley farm ‘people of color’ Saturdays stalls
item.description: A civil rights complaint against UC Berkeley's Gill Tract Farm alleges it only allowed "people of color" on Saturdays. The case has stalled amid a significant backlog in the Department of Education’s Office for Civil Rights.

item.title: Scholars question University of California ‘anti-Palestinian racism’ study
item.description: Witnessing 'racism' includes seeing a social media post about it.

item.title: ASU professor petitions Arizona Supreme Court after DEI training lawsuit blocked
item.description: Arizona State University professor Owen Anderson is asking the state Supreme Court to hear his case after a lower court dismissed his lawsuit challenging mandatory ideological DEI training. item.title: Texas opens new website for reporting alleged DEI violations at public colleges
